jamie_support: Customer (Acme onboarding) reports their embeddings suddenly changed size after they pinned a model. Their index expects 768 but responses are 1536 — ingestion failing with shape mismatch. Can we triage?

ashley_research: Can you paste the exact API request + the returned model metadata (if available)? Are they pinning an alias or an exact variant id? :eyes:

jamie_support: Here is the cURL they ran:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-stable","input":"hello world"}'
```
And the truncated response they pasted back: 
```json
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.0012,0.0023,...(1536 floats)...],"model":"redwood-embed-stable-v2-q8_1536"}],"model":"redwood-embed-stable-v2-q8_1536"}
```
So the model in the payload resolved to a v2 quantized variant with vec_dim=1536.

ashley_research: That explains the dim change — the alias resolved to a 1536-dim variant. Did they pin the alias string (e.g., `redwood-embed-stable@latest`) instead of an immutable variant id?

mike_ops: Check routing logs — if their reserved capacity or fallback routing used a different pool, it could surface a different variant. Also confirm whether an alias swap or canary promoted during migration.

jamie_support: I pulled their account pin metadata: pinned_to = "redwood-embed-stable@2026-02-12" (customer thought this was stable). The model resolution shows target_variant = "redwood-embed-stable-v2-q8_1536".

eva_eng: Looks like a model migration promoted a v2 variant under the same alias during our rollout. We should have prevented alias promotion when vec_dim != previous_dim. Root cause theory: alias swap happened without a compatibility check.

ashley_research: Workarounds: 1) Have customer pin the explicit immutable variant id (e.g., redwood-embed-stable-v1-immutable) or 2) we roll the alias back to the 768 variant. Also advise reindexing their vectors after the rollback.

deployment-bot: Alias rollback job queued. action=rollback alias=redwood-embed-stable target=redwood-embed-stable-v1 status=started at=1739993000

deployment-bot: Alias rollback completed. action=rollback alias=redwood-embed-stable target=redwood-embed-stable-v1 status=completed at=1739993045

mike_ops: I confirmed routing logs — requests from the customer's org hit the promoted variant between 1739992468 and 1739993045. Rollback has restored previous variant.

jamie_support: Told customer to retry ingestion and reindex. They re-ran and report success — index accepted vectors at 768 again. They're asking for an incident summary and compensation.

eva_eng: I'll open an internal bug: "alias-swap-preserve-schema". Action items: add preflight check that prevents alias point-to-point swaps where core embedding schema (vec_dim) changes without a warning; add an API header `x-embed-dim` in responses so callers can detect schema mismatches early; add a post-deploy validation step for alias promotions.

jamie_support: Drafted customer message: "We identified that an alias promotion during a model rollout caused your alias to resolve to a variant with a different embedding dimension. We rolled back the alias and recommend reindexing; we're adding safeguards to prevent recurrence. We'll follow up with a detailed postmortem and a credit. Apologies for the disruption." :handshake:

ashley_research: Also suggest we add a server-side check to reject pinned alias assignments if the pinned alias would change vec_dim for an org that already has indexed data.

jamie_support: Thanks all — closing this Slack thread and creating the support ticket with timeline + artifacts.
